about.title: Shafter Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Shafter residents often travel to larger Kern County facilities for specialized care, and most of those visits go the way they should. But when a provider misses a clear warning sign, operates on the wrong site, or sends someone home with the wrong medication, the harm can be lasting. California law treats these cases differently than a typical injury claim — there are shorter deadlines, a required pre-suit notice, and rules around expert review that make early action important. LawProactive doesn't practice law or decide the merits of any case. We simply listen to what happened, ask a few questions, and if it looks like a fit, connect you with an independent attorney in our network who takes medical malpractice cases on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless they recover money for you. A bad outcome by itself doesn't mean malpractice occurred, but you deserve a clear answer from someone qualified to give one.

whyChoose.title: Why Timing and Process Matter in Shafter Malpractice Cases

items.title: Strict Filing Deadlines Under MICRA
items.desc: California generally gives one year from when the harm is discovered, and never more than three years from the original injury, to bring a claim. Waiting too long to talk to someone can permanently close the door, so acting sooner rather than later matters.

items.title: A 90-Day Notice Comes First
items.desc: Before a malpractice lawsuit can be filed in California, the provider typically must receive written notice at least 90 days in advance. An attorney familiar with this step can make sure it's handled correctly and on time.

items.title: Expert Review Is Almost Always Required
items.desc: Because a bad outcome alone doesn't prove malpractice, California cases generally need a qualified medical expert to establish that the standard of care was broken. The attorneys in our network work with the right experts to evaluate whether a claim holds up.

items.question: How do I know if what happened to me in Shafter was actually malpractice?
items.answer: Not every complication or disappointing result is malpractice — sometimes medicine simply doesn't go as hoped. The question is whether the provider deviated from what a reasonably careful professional would have done in the same situation. An independent attorney, often working with a medical expert, is best positioned to make that call after reviewing your records.

items.question: Do I have to travel outside Shafter to get help with a malpractice claim?
items.answer: Many Shafter residents already travel to nearby Kern County providers for specialized medical care, and the attorneys in our network are used to working with patients throughout the region. You can typically handle much of the process by phone or video, and LawProactive's connection service itself is free no matter where in Shafter you're located.

items.question: What does the statutory cap on damages mean for my case?
items.answer: California law caps non-economic damages — compensation for things like pain and suffering — in medical malpractice cases, and that cap amount rises each year under current law. Economic damages, such as medical bills and lost income, are generally not subject to this cap. An attorney can walk you through how this applies to your specific situation.
